flashcard_questions.a: Hardwood comes from deciduous trees (harder, denser, slower growing). Softwood comes from coniferous trees (faster growing, cheaper, softer).
flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between hardwood and softwood?

flashcard_questions.a: Low carbon steel (mild steel), cast iron, high carbon steel (tool steel).
Thermoforming: softens when heated, can be reshaped. Thermosetting: sets permanently, cannot be reshaped.
flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between thermoforming and thermosetting polymers?

flashcard_questions.a: Malleability: can be hammered into shape. Ductility: can be drawn into wire. Both involve reshaping without breaking.
flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between malleability and ductility?

flashcard_questions.a: Absorbency, density, fusibility, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity (any three).
flashcard_questions.q: Name three physical properties of materials.
